Most technical indicators die in publication. Larry Connors's R3 didn't. It got copied, audited, and shipped to ETF traders for 15 years.

The rule is 4 lines long. It only buys panics inside an uptrend.

Here's the complete logic, no black box:

🔹 200-DAY UPTREND FILTER. Only consider longs when price is above its 200-day SMA. Dips in an uptrend revert. Dips in a downtrend continue.
🔹 RSI(2) OVERSOLD. Use a 2-period RSI, not the 14-period default. RSI(2) captures short-term panic the standard reading sleeps through.
🔹 THREE-RED FILTER. RSI(2) has to decline 3 days in a row. First reading below 60, third reading below 10. This filters noise from real flushes.
🔹 MEAN-REVERT EXIT. Close the long when RSI(2) crosses back above 70 (or above 30 on the faster variant).
🔹 LIQUID UNIVERSE. Designed for liquid ETFs and large-cap equities. Few-day holds.
🔹 FULLY MECHANICAL. No discretion. Codeable in under 50 lines.

Source: Connors and Alvarez (2009), High Probability ETF Trading, Chapter 4. Independent backtests at QuantifiedStrategies, Easycators, and TradingView. Educational use only.
